messages:
maria: Heads up — we need a short ops playbook for granting short-lived per-API-key overrides for partner/internal keys during incidents. Can we align on guardrails + console UX?

alex: +1. Core goals: auditable, reversible, TTL-bounded, granular (per-key or per-service), and easy to reason about from the console. No silent bypasses.

thomas: Implementation idea: key metadata gets an `override` object: `{expiry_ts, reason, approved_by, limit_delta, audit_id}`. New internal API: `POST /internal/keys/:key_id/override` payload `{ttl_seconds, new_rps, reason, approver}`. Only callable by ops/service accounts.

sophia: Console flow: modal when applying override that requires justification, optional JIRA link, shows projected cost/QPS delta, and a preview of client-side impact. Audit log line visible on key details page.

alex: Safety controls: 1) automatic rollback at expiry, 2) snapshot current limits before applying (for rollback), 3) two-step approval for >50% increase or >1000 RPS, 4) rate-limit the number of concurrent active overrides per account. Emit telemetry event `key.override.applied`.

ops-bot: FYI: reconciliation job runs every 30s to clear expired overrides and reapply original limits. Logs: `INFO reconcile: key=xxx expired=true rollback_ok=true`.

maria: Q: how do we handle partner integrations where the same key is used by multiple internal services? Do we allow service-scoped overrides?

thomas: Add optional `scope` param: `service:<id>` or `all`. Default to `service_scoped` (i.e., only override for tokens used by a particular service tag). Explicit `all` requires manual ops approval + audit ticket.

sophia: Edge-case: CDN/gateway caches might keep old rate-limit decisions for a few seconds. Recommend a 60s grace window for rollback where we send advanced warning event `key.override.will_expire` and a 30s pre-rolloff 'throttle ramp' in the gateway to avoid sudden connection drops. :warning: 

alex: Telemetry schema (draft): `key.override.applied {key_id, approver, ttl_s, delta_rps, scope, audit_id, timestamp}` and `key.override.reverted {key_id, reason, rollback_ts}`. These should be present in per-key dashboards and trigger regression alerts if increased error rate or latency.

sophia: Minimal CLI example for ops (internal only):

```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.local/keys/abcd1234/override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"ttl_seconds":3600, "new_rps":5000, "reason":"incident spike - analytics", "approver":"maria"}'
```

maria: UX note: modal should require checkbox "I confirm I own the mitigation plan" and an optional rollback checklist link. Also show cost estimate for token usage during override.

infra-bot: Rolling out a feature flag `key_override_api_v1` to staging tomorrow. Gate: only service accounts with role `ops_override` can hit endpoint.

alex: Action items: (1) thomas to sketch API + proto PR by EOD Friday (2) sophia to produce modal mock + audit-log UI by Wednesday (3) infra to add telemetry hooks and reconciliation job checks (owner: infra-bot) (4) ops to write short playbook doc (owner: maria).

maria: I'll spin up a 48h pilot with analytics-ingest partner once infra flag is in staging. Tagging @oncall for visibility. If no objections, we'll proceed. :thumbsup:

thomas: quick note — keep override records immutable once applied (new record per change) so audit trail is reliable.

ops-bot: ACK — will emit `audit_id` on apply and include link to internal ticket if provided.

alex: Looks good. One more constraint: limit override lifespan to max 7 days via policy (configurable). Any longer requires leadership sign-off and manual entry in governance log.

maria: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll create the GH issue with the checklist and link to these notes.
